Answer: B
Reason: The CT images (Figures 4-6) demonstrate massive tracheobronchomegaly with markedly dilated trachea and main bronchi, alongside multiple large intrapulmonary cavities/cystic spaces connected to the airways, which are pathognomonic features of Mounier-Kuhn Syndrome. While the X-ray classifier was non-specific, the distinct morphological findings on the provided cross-sectional imaging confirm this rare congenital disorder over other options like bronchiectasis or ABPA which lack such profound central airway dilation.
